title: The termite and the treaty
hookLine: the sirah says the boycott document was eaten by termites except the name of Allah

cards: Somewhere inside the Ka'ba, in the dark, the document still hangs, the one that has kept a whole clan hungry in the valley. Quraysh have no reason to take it down and read it; they know what it says.
And all that time, the sirah says, something small has been at work on it, without anyone noticing. Not a person. Not an army.

teach.b: Ibn Ishaq tells it like this.

teach.h: GO AND LOOK, SAID ABU TALIB.
teach.b: The Prophet, peace be upon him, told his uncle Abu Talib that God had sent the termite against the document, and that it had eaten every word of injustice and broken ties in it, leaving only the place where the name of God was written.
Abu Talib asked him: did your Lord tell you this? Yes, he said. So Abu Talib walked out of the valley to the gathering of Quraysh and made them an offer.
My nephew says this. Go and look. If he's lying, I'll hand him over to you.
If he's telling the truth, end this boycott. They took down the document and found it as he had said. Notice what was left.
The document opened, as Quraysh's writings of the time did, with the words bismika Allahumma: in your name, O God. Those words were all that remained.
The cruelty had been eaten; the name stood. In fairness, the reports differ on the details, and some versions say the opposite: that the name of God was what the termite took, and the rest was left.

The sirah also tells of Meccans already working to end the boycott, which is tomorrow's story. But in Ibn Ishaq's telling the picture is clear. Words written to starve a family turned out to be fragile.
The name of God, written at the top almost as a formality, outlasted them.

how: Muslims retell the story of the termite and the boycott document in sirah lessons, and some teachers point to it as one of the signs given to the Prophet in Mecca.

games.why: Ibn Ishaq says Abu Talib staked his nephew on it; Quraysh looked and found the document as he'd said.

practice: Think back over a hard stretch in your life, a bad year, a loss, a time when something unfair had you boxed in, and let what has faded fall away.

Look only at what's still standing from that time: a friendship that held, a habit of prayer or kindness that started then, a sentence someone said that you still carry. If you pray, you can give thanks for it in your own words.

wordCard.voice: Bismika Allahumma: in your name, O God. The sirah says termites ate the boycott document, leaving only these words standing. Today's word.

orig.note: Arabic: in your name, O God, the words at the head of the document that the sirah says remained.

carryVoice: Your line: only the name remained. A small insect, and a long cruelty undone. Until tomorrow.
